vegan = eating no animal products, including milk, eggs and honey
pescatarian = a person who does not eat meat but does eat fish
flexitarian = a person who mainly eats plant food but occasionally eats meat
intolerance = difficulty digesting a food, causing discomfort but not a full allergy
nutrient = a substance in food that the body needs, such as a vitamin or protein
malnutrition = poor health caused by not having enough of the right foods
undernourished = not getting enough food or nutrients to stay healthy
obesity = the state of having so much body fat that it harms health
calorie intake = the amount of energy you get from food and drink
empty calories = energy from food that offers little nutritional value
crash diet = a very strict, short-term eating plan that cuts food severely
fad diet = a fashionable eating plan that promises fast results with little evidence
yo-yo dieting = repeatedly losing weight and then gaining it again
portion control = choosing sensible amounts of food rather than eating until the plate is empty
fasting = going without food for a set time, often for health or religion
intermittent fasting = an eating pattern with regular periods of not eating
supplement = a pill or powder taken to add nutrients to your diet
antioxidant = a substance in some foods thought to protect cells from damage
probiotic = a food or drink containing live bacteria that may help the gut
fluid intake = the amount of liquid you drink
